items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: He took lessons from you, too, here in Chicago. Yeah, he sure did.

ctx.x: It wouldn't take you long, I don't believe, to get back in shape as far as the... I don't think so, no. I mean, anybody really knows something, as they say, you never forget it. No, you never forget it. Like they say, for instance, riding a bicycle, if you've never ridden for ten years, you can get on a bicycle. Try to get on a bicycle and go right on. And they say, you can't swim like me, you're like me. But they say, if you once learned to swim when you were a kid, maybe fifty years later, somebody will push…

But still, it'd be better than almost anybody can do now. Oh, yeah. I've never heard, I'm sure. Yeah, these fellas are playing now. I don't know. I'm not knocking, I'm not knocking like that. But, I don't know, they don't seem to get the right bass on, you know, on trombone. It seem like they're off some way. It seem like they're way back. And sometimes I pick up, sometime on the radio, hear some fellas playing, and he's alright, but there's a few of them, see? Yeah. And the majority, they look like as many bands…
There's one other New Orleans tromboneist here, Albert Wynn. Do you know that?
